claims.text: daedalus.eval -- a small, private eval harness for the distillation thesis.
claims.why: The size and privacy of the harness cannot be verified from this chunk; only the module header and imports are present.

claims.text: The claim under test: a *distilled semantic slice* (the focus symbol/file plus its dependency + caller neighborhood) carries enough context to act on a target at a fraction of the tokens of a naive whole-repo concatenation (Repomix / Gitingest style). "Distillation beats concatenation."
claims.why: The definition of a distilled semantic slice and the comparison logic live in the harness and tasks modules; this chunk contains only the statement, not the implementation.

claims.text: This is a **private, directional** eval, NOT SWE-bench.
claims.why: Whether the eval is private and directional cannot be determined from this chunk; no task definitions or comparison methodology are present.

claims.text: Tier 1 (deterministic, no LLM -- the rigorous core): for each labelled task measure slice **recall** (did the distilled slice actually contain the symbols a competent answer needs?) and **compression** (how much smaller than the whole repo?).
claims.why: run_tier1 is imported from .harness, not defined here; the actual measurements and their determinism cannot be observed from this chunk.

claims.text: Recall is *necessary, not sufficient* -- it proves the slice didn't drop load-bearing context.
claims.why: This is an interpretive claim about the semantics of the recall metric; the metric's implementation is in .harness and not visible here.

claims.text: Tier 2 (opt-in, needs a runtime): ask the same question against the distilled slice (A) and against the whole-repo concat (B) via a model, and compare task-success and tokens.
claims.why: run_tier2 is imported from .harness; the comparison logic and token accounting are not in this chunk.

claims.text: The win is A ~= B success at a fraction of B's tokens.
claims.why: This is a success criterion for the eval; whether the implementation enforces or evaluates it cannot be checked from this chunk.

claims.text: Gated: skipped cleanly when no provider is available.
claims.why: The gating logic is inside run_tier2 in .harness; this chunk only imports the function and does not show the provider check or skip behaviour.

claims.why: This chunk contains no imports from structcore and no mutation code; the isolation claim cannot be verified from this file alone.
